note: robots.txt product tokens of other AI agents, compiled for Remorsearch UX QA from each operator's own documentation (doc). fetch_on_behalf: an AI agent that fetches a page because a person asked it something. This reader is also an AI agent fetching for a person, so when no robots.txt group names RemorsearchUXQA, a group naming one of these tokens that disallows the path is honoured as if it named RemorsearchUXQA: the URL stops as opted_out with the reason robots:ai_agent:<token>. Such a group only adds disallows; its Allow lines never lift a '*' disallow, and a group naming RemorsearchUXQA decides alone. training_or_index: a crawler that collects pages for model training or an AI search index; a group naming it that disallows the path is recorded as a signal (ai_training_disallow), never a stop. Tokens match case-insensitively on the product token. verified: the token and its purpose were read on the operator's page on checked_at (read_via 'direct', or 'search_index' when only the search index of that page could be reached); unverified tokens are still honoured, because honouring one can only add stops. Why: Naver's blog and cafe robots.txt reportedly block AI training and search crawlers since 2025-07 (a signal under this rule; the expected outcome stays unknown until a live robots check), Coupang's robots.txt reportedly names ChatGPT-User (a stop under this rule), and the PIPC's 2025 generative-AI guide reportedly treats a robots.txt block as a clear refusal.
